
# Conceptual Foundations of Dynamic Structural Equation Modeling

## Example Data For Illustrations

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47.5%"}


* Data from a study by @Bolzenkoetter2024
* Initial study investigated the effect of a detached mindfulness intervention on repetitive negative thinking (RNT) and affect
  * *N* = 100 participants engaged in a 5-day long baseline phase with ESM assessment, followed by a 5-day intervention phase
  * Intervention was either (0) active control ("normal" mindfulness exercises) or (1) detached mindfulness exercise

![](./img/bolzen_study.png){width="100%"}

* Found effect of mindfulness intervention and active control on positive affect, negative affect and RNT

:::

::: {.column width="5%"}

:::

::: {.column width="47.5%"}

* We will be investigating the temporal dynamics of positive affect in the workshop

## Common Ground: Two-Level AR(1) using `lme4`


::: {.vspace}
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}


#### Decomposition of Between- and Within-level

$$
Y_{it}^{pmc} = Y_{it} - \overline{Y_i}
$$

$Y_{it}$ is centered at the observed person mean!


::: {.vspace}
:::

#### Within-level model

$$
Y_{it} = \overline{Y}_i + \phi_i Y_{i(t-1)}^{pmc} + \zeta_{it} \\
\zeta_{it} \sim \operatorname{N}(0, \sigma_{\zeta}^2)
$$ 

::: {.vspace}
:::

#### Between-level model

$$
\begin{matrix}
\overline{Y}_i  = \gamma_{\overline{Y}}  + \upsilon_{\overline{Y} i} \\
\phi_i = \gamma_{\phi} + \upsilon_{\phi i}
\end{matrix}
$$ 

$$
\text{with}\ \mathbf{\upsilon} \sim \operatorname{MVN}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{\Sigma})
$$ 


:::

::: {.column width="10%"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{tikz}
%| label: lme4-ar1
%| echo: false
%| fig-width: 3
%| fig-height: 3
%| out-width: "80%"
\newlength{\Radius}
\setlength\Radius{4em}
\usetikzlibrary{shapes, positioning, calc, decorations.markings, chains, scopes}
\begin{tikzpicture}[

  	},

  	  inner sep = 0pt, minimum size = 5mm
  	},
  	var/.style = {
  	  <->, thick, > = {stealth[]}, bend right = 270, looseness = 2
  	},
  	cov/.style = {
  	  <->, thick, > = {stealth[]}, bend right = 300
  	},
  	% style to add a circle in the middle of a path
    random/.style = {
      postaction = {
        decorate, decoration = {
          markings,
          mark = at position .5 with {
            \draw[fill = black] circle[radius = 2pt];
          }
        }
      }
    },

      postaction = {decorate, decoration = {
        markings,
        mark = at position .2 with {
          \draw[fill = black] circle[radius = 2pt];}
        }
      }
    },
  	]

    % draw decomposition
    \node  [manifest]  (y1t)  {$Y_{it}$};
    \node  [latent]  (y1wt)  [above = 4em of y1t]  {$Y_{it}^{pmc}$};
    \node  [latent]  (mu1)  [below = 4em of y1t]  {$\overline{Y_{i}}$};
    
    \node  [coordinate] (c_decomp1) at ($(y1wt)!0.5!(y1wt)$) {};

    % draw paths
    \draw  [path]  (y1wt)  to node  []  {}  (y1t);
    \draw  [path]  (mu1)  to node  []  {}  (y1t);
    
    
    % within-level model
    \node  [latent]  (y1wt-1) [right = 2.5em of y1wt] {$Y_{i(t-1)}^{pmc}$};
    \node  [latent]  (y1wt)  [right = 5em of y1wt-1]  {$Y_{it}^{pmc}$};
    \node  [latent]  (zeta1t)  [right = 2.5em of y1wt]  {$\zeta_{it}$};% draw paths
    \draw  [path]  (zeta1t)  to node  []  {}  (y1wt);
    
    \draw  [path, postaction = random]  (y1wt-1)  to node  []  {$\phi_{i}$}  (y1wt);
    \draw  [var]  (zeta1t.30)  to node  []  {$\sigma^2_{\zeta}$}  (zeta1t.330);
    
    
    % between-level model
    % center the between-level model below the within-level model,
    % at the height of mu1
    \coordinate  (within-mid)  at  ($(y1wt-1)!0.5!(zeta1t)$);
    \coordinate  (between-mid)  at  (within-mid |- mu1);
    \node  [latent]  (mu_1)  at  ($(between-mid) + (-2.5em, 0)$)  {$\overline{Y_{i}}$};
    \node  [latent]  (phi1_11)  [right = 1em of mu_1]  {$\phi_{i}$};



    \node  [coordinate]  (c1)  [above = 2em of mu_1]  {};
    \node  [coordinate]  (c2)  [above = 2em of phi1_11]  {}; \draw  [path]  (c1)  to node  []  {}  (mu_1);
    \draw  [path]  (c2)  to node  []  {}  (phi1_11); \draw  [thick]  (c1)  --  (c2);
    
        \node  [draw=none, above = 3em of c_decomp1, inner sep=1pt, text height=1.5ex, text depth=0.3ex] (decomp) {Decomposition};
    \node  [draw=none, above = 3em of within-mid, inner sep=1pt, text height=1.5ex, text depth=0.3ex] (decomp) {Within-level model};
    \node  [draw=none, above = 5em of between-mid, inner sep=1pt, text height=1.5ex, text depth=0.3ex] (decomp) {Between-level model};
        
  
\end{tikzpicture}
```

* Individuals differ in their
  * stable person mean
  * autoregressive effect (dynamics)
* Residuals on the within-level (*innovations*, $\zeta_{it}$) are assumed to be i.i.d

## Model Estimation

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "50%"}

```{r echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)

# create lagged variable for lme4
bolzen_baseline <- bolzen %>%
  filter(phase == "b") %>% # select baseline phase
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    posaff_pmc = posaff - mean(posaff, na.rm = T),
    posaff_pmc_lag1 = lag(posaff_pmc)
  )

# model in lme4
lme4_fit1 <- lmer(
  posaff ~ 1 + posaff_pmc_lag1 +
    (1 + posaff_pmc_lag1 | id),
  data = bolzen_baseline
)
```

* We need to create a lagged variable to use as predictor and center it at the person mean
* As `lme4` does not allow `NA` in the predictor, the first observation for every individual is dropped

:::

::: {.column width="5%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}


```{r echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
summary(lme4_fit1)
```

:::
::::

## Model Results I: Between-person level

```{r echo=FALSE, eval = TRUE}
# get model coefficients
gamma0_mu <- fixef(lme4_fit1)["(Intercept)"]
gamma0_phi <- fixef(lme4_fit1)["posaff_pmc_lag1"]
vc <- VarCorr(lme4_fit1)
sigma_mu <- attr(vc$id, "stddev")["(Intercept)"]
sigma_phi <- attr(vc$id, "stddev")["posaff_pmc_lag1"]
cor_mu_phi <- attr(vc$id, "correlation")["(Intercept)", "posaff_pmc_lag1"]
sigma_zeta <- attr(vc, "sc")
```

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "50%"}

<!-- $$ -->
<!-- \begin{matrix} -->
<!-- \gamma_{\mu} =& `r gamma0_mu` \\ -->
<!-- \phi_i =& `r gamma0_phi` -->
<!-- \end{matrix} -->
<!-- $$ -->
<!-- $$ -->
<!-- \begin{matrix} -->
<!-- \sigma_{\upsilon_{\mu i}} = `r sigma_mu` \\ -->
<!-- \sigma_{\upsilon_{\phi i}} = `r sigma_phi` \\ -->
<!-- \rho_{\upsilon_{\mu i}, \upsilon_{\phi i}} = `r cor_mu_phi` \\ -->
<!-- \sigma_{\zeta} = `r sigma_zeta` -->
<!-- \end{matrix} -->
<!-- $$ -->


$$
Y_{it} = (`r round(gamma0_mu,2)` + \upsilon_{\mu i}) + (`r round(gamma0_phi,2)` + \upsilon_{\phi i}) Y_{i(t-1)}^{pmc} + \zeta_{it}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\upsilon_{\mu i} &\sim \operatorname{N}(0, `r round(sigma_mu^2,2)`) \\
\upsilon_{\phi i} &\sim \operatorname{N}(0, `r round(sigma_phi^2,2)`) \\
\rho_{\mu_i, \phi_i} &= `r round(cor_mu_phi,2)`
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center

# fixed effects
fe <- fixef(lme4_fit1)

# random effects (deviations from fixed effects), combined into per-id intercept/slope
re <- ranef(lme4_fit1)$id
coefs <- coef(lme4_fit1)$id  # this already gives fixed + random per id
coefs$id <- rownames(coefs)
names(coefs)[1:2] <- c("intercept", "slope")

# data range for drawing lines (use actual range of the predictor)
x_range <- range(bolzen_baseline$posaff_pmc_lag1, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot() +
  # individual lines
  geom_abline(
    data = coefs,
    aes(intercept = intercept, slope = slope, group = id),
    color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # fixed-effect (average) line
  geom_abline(
    intercept = fe[1], slope = fe[2],
    color = "green4", linewidth = 1.5
  ) +
  xlim(x_range) +
  ylim(range(bolzen_baseline$posaff, na.rm = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    x = "Positive affect (lag 1, person-mean centered)",
    y = "Positive affect",
    title = "Individual (grey) vs. fixed-effect (green) slopes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16))
```


:::

::: {.column width="5%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}


```{r echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
summary(lme4_fit1)
```

## Model Results II: Within-person level


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "50%"}

$$
Y_{it} = (`r round(gamma0_mu,2)` + \upsilon_{\mu i}) + (`r round(gamma0_phi,2)` + \upsilon_{\phi i}) Y_{i(t-1)}^{pmc} + \zeta_{it}
$$

$$
\zeta_{it} \sim \operatorname{N}(0, `r round(sigma_zeta^2,2)`)
$$

* Innovations $\zeta_{it}$ are assumed to come from the same distribution for all individuals

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center
# model in lme4 with nas
lme4_fit1 <- lmer(
  posaff ~ 1 + posaff_pmc_lag1 +
    (1 + posaff_pmc_lag1 | id),
  data = bolzen_baseline,
  na.action = na.exclude
)
bolzen_baseline$fitted <- predict(lme4_fit1)

# pick a handful of individuals to keep it readable
set.seed(14)
sample_ids <- sample(unique(bolzen_baseline$id), 4)

bolzen_baseline %>%
  filter(id %in% sample_ids) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = obs_counter, y = posaff)) +   # replace `time` with your actual time/obs-index variable
  geom_line(color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(color = "grey40", size = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fitted), color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, ncol = 2, nrow = 3) +
  labs(y = "Positive affect", x = "Time",
       title = paste0("Observed (grey) vs. predicted (blue) positive affect for ", length(sample_ids),  " IDs")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16))
```


:::

:::

## Two-Level AR(1) using `mlts`


::: {.vspace}
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}


#### Decomposition of Between- and Within-level

$$
Y_{it}^{w} = Y_{it} - \mu_{i}
$$

$Y_{it}$ is centered at the **latent** person mean!


::: {.vspace}
:::

#### Within-level model

$$
Y_{it}^w = \phi_i Y_{i(t-1)}^{w} + \zeta_{it} \\
\zeta_{it} \sim N(0, \sigma_{\zeta,i}^2)
$$ 

::: {.vspace}
:::

#### Between-level model

$$
\begin{matrix}
\mu_i  = \gamma_{\mu}  + \upsilon_{\mu i} \\
\phi_i = \gamma_{\phi} + \upsilon_{\phi i} \\
ln(\sigma_{\zeta i}^2) = \gamma_{ln(\sigma^2_\zeta)} + \upsilon_{ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta,i})}
\end{matrix}
$$ 

$$
\text{with}\ \mathbf{\upsilon} \sim \operatorname{MVN}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{\Sigma})
$$ 


:::

::: {.column width="10%"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

## Model Building

```{r}
#| include: false
options(width = 120)  # increase from default ~80
```



```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

library(mlts)

# model in mlts
mlts_m1 <- mlts_model(q = 1, max_lag = 1)
mlts_m1[, c("Model", "Level", "Type", "Param_Label", "isRandom")] # inspect
```

* `mlts_model()` returns a data frame with rows corresponding to parameters in the model (parameter names follow DSEM convention)
  * Our AR(1) model has 9 parameters: 3 fixed effects, 3 random effect SDs, and 3 correlations between random effects
* The argument `q` controls the number of time-varying constructs
* The argument `max_lag` controls the maximum number of autoregressive effects (maximum is 3)




## Helper Functions for Model Building

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "40%"}

* `mlts_paths()` draws a path diagram of the model using the package `diagram`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mlts_paths(mlts_m1)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

mlts_paths(mlts_m1, height = 5.5, width = 8.5, cex_b = 1.1)
```

* Alternatively, `mlts_model_paths()` draws a `tikz`-model and prints to pdf (for LaTeX users, but does currently not handle all modeling options)

:::

::: {.column width="10%"}
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

* `mlts_model_formula()` creates a pdf with model formula in matrix notation and prints to pdf (also keeps LaTeX code)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mlts_model_formula(mlts_m1)
```

::: {.center}
**Decomposition**
:::
$$
\begin{gathered} \begin{bmatrix}
y_{1, it} \\
\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}
\mu_{1,i} \\
\end{bmatrix}
+
\begin{bmatrix}
y_{1, it}^w \\
\end{bmatrix} \end{gathered}
$$

::: {.center}
**Within-level model**
:::
$$
\begin{gathered} \begin{bmatrix}
y_{1, it}^w \\
\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \phi_{(1)11,i} \\ \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_{1,i(t - 1)}^w \\ \end{bmatrix} +  \begin{bmatrix} \zeta_{1, it} \\ \end{bmatrix} ,\\ 
\text{with}~\zeta_{1,it} \sim \operatorname{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\zeta_{1},i})  \end{gathered}
$$

::: {.center}
**Between-level model**
:::
$$
\begin{gathered} \begin{bmatrix} \mu_{1,i}\\
\phi_{(1)11,i}\\
\ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1},i})\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \gamma_{0,\mu_{1}}\\
\gamma_{0,\phi_{(1)11}}\\
\gamma_{0,\ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1}})}\\ \end{bmatrix} +
  \begin{bmatrix} \upsilon_{\mu_{1},i}\\
\upsilon_{\phi_{(1)11},i}\\
\upsilon_{\ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1}}),i}\\ \end{bmatrix} ,\\ 
\text{with}~
  \upsilon_{i} \sim \operatorname{MVN}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{\Omega})  \end{gathered}
$$

:::
::::

## Model Estimation

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "35%"}


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mlts_fit1 <- mlts_fit(
  model = mlts_m1, # model object
  data = bolzen,   # data set
  id = "id",       # id variable
  ts = "posaff",   # time series construct
  iter = 2000      # number of MCMC iterations
)
```

* For a simple (V)AR model, we only need to provide the model from `mlts_model()`, the data frame, an `id` variable, and the time series construct
* The default number of MCMC iterations is 500, we set it a bit higher here to guarantee good mixing
* The function preprocesses the data on its own and passes all model information to Stan, where the model is fit with Markov Chain Monte Carlo



:::
:::  {.column width = "10%"}
:::



:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "35%"}

* The `summary()` function shows general information about the time-series constructs and model convergence first
  * `mlts` allows for `NA` in the time-series constructs, therefore we are using all $n = `r nrow(bolzen_baseline)`$ observations
  * Check ESS, Rhat, and divergent transitions!
* MCMC traceplots can be obtained using `rstan` (the backend behind `mlts`) or the package `bayesplot`, but follow internal naming as of now
<!-- * For example, fixed effects are stored as a parameter named `gammas` -->

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-align: center

rstan::traceplot(mlts_fit1$stanfit,
                 pars = "gammas")
```

## Model Results II: Model Parameters

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

# fixed effects
gamma0_mu_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "mu_1", "mean"]
gamma0_phi_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "phi(1)_11", "mean"]
gamma0_ln_sigma_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "ln.sigma2_1", "mean"]

# random effects SDs
sigma_mu_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "sigma_mu_1", "mean"]
sigma_phi_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "sigma_phi(1)_11", "mean"]
sigma_ln_sigma_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "sigma_ln.sigma2_1", "mean"]

# random effect cors
cor_mu_phi_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "r_mu_1.phi(1)_11", "mean"]
cor_mu_ln.sigma_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "r_mu_1.ln.sigma2_1", "mean"]
cor_phi_ln.sigma_mlts <- mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]][mlts_fit1[["pop.pars.summary"]]$Param == "r_phi(1)_11.ln.sigma2_1", "mean"]
```


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "35%"}

#### Within-level model

$$
Y_{it}^w = `r round(gamma0_phi_mlts, 2)` ~ Y_{i(t-1)}^{w} + \zeta_{it} \\
\zeta_{it} \sim N(0, \underbrace{`r round(exp(gamma0_ln_sigma_mlts), 2)`}_{\text{This is exp($`r round(gamma0_ln_sigma_mlts, 3)`$)!}})
$$ 

* If innovation variance is person-specific, it needs to be on the log-scale (otherwise we could get negative values) $\rightarrow$ `ln.sigma2_1` needs to be exponentiated!
  
#### Between-level model (variances + correlations)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "50%"}


$$
\begin{aligned}
\upsilon_{\mu i} &\sim \operatorname{N}(0, `r round(sigma_mu_mlts,2)`^2) \\
\upsilon_{\phi i} &\sim \operatorname{N}(0, `r round(sigma_phi_mlts,2)`^2) \\
\upsilon_{\ln(\sigma^2) i} &\sim \operatorname{N}(0, `r round(sigma_ln_sigma_mlts,2)`^2)
\end{aligned}
$$ 
:::
::: {.column width = "50%"}
$$
\left[
\begin{array}{ccc}
 & & \vphantom{1^2}  \\
`r round(cor_mu_phi_mlts, 2)` &  & \vphantom{1^2} \\
`r round(cor_mu_ln.sigma_mlts, 2)` & `r round(cor_phi_ln.sigma_mlts, 2)` & \hphantom{1.0} \vphantom{1^2}
\end{array}
\right]
$$  
:::
::::

:::
:::  {.column width = "5%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "60%"}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

summary(mlts_fit1)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: asis

color_nth_occurrence <- function(text, anchor, n, color = "blue") {
  # collapse to one string so occurrence counting works across lines
  full_text <- paste(text, collapse = "\n")
  
  pattern <- paste0(anchor, "\\s*\\S+")
  matches <- gregexpr(pattern, full_text)[[1]]
  match_lengths <- attr(matches, "match.length")
  
  if (length(matches) < n || matches[1] == -1) {
    warning("Fewer than ", n, " occurrences found")
    return(text)
  }
  
  # extract the nth match
  start <- matches[n]
  end <- start + match_lengths[n] - 1
  matched_str <- substr(full_text, start, end)
  
  # split matched string into anchor part and value part
  value_start <- regexpr("\\S+$", matched_str)
  anchor_part <- substr(matched_str, 1, value_start - 1)
  value_part <- substr(matched_str, value_start, nchar(matched_str))
  
  colored <- paste0(anchor_part, '<span style="color:', color, ';">', value_part, '</span>')
  
  # rebuild the string
  new_text <- paste0(
    substr(full_text, 1, start - 1),
    colored,
    substr(full_text, end + 1, nchar(full_text))
  )
  
  strsplit(new_text, "\n")[[1]]
}


summary_lines <- capture.output(summary(mlts_fit1))

# color lines
# summary_lines <- gsub(
#   "(ln\\.sigma2_1\\s+)(\\S+)",
#   '\\1<span style="color:blue;">\\2</span>',
#   summary_lines
# )

summary_lines <- color_nth_occurrence(summary_lines, "ln\\.sigma2_1", n = 1, color = "blue")

cat('<div class="cell-output cell-output-stdout">\n<pre><code>')
cat("[...]\n")
cat(summary_lines[10:32], sep = "\n")
cat('</code></pre>\n</div>')
# cat("[...]")
```

## Model Results III: Random Effect Distributions

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

# model-implied distributions of the person-specific parameters:
# N(fixed effect, SD of random effect)
re_params <- tibble(
  param = factor(
    c("Mean~level~(mu[i])",
      "Autoregression~(phi[i])",
      "Log~innovation~variance~(ln~sigma[i]^2)"),
    levels = c("Mean~level~(mu[i])",
               "Autoregression~(phi[i])",
               "Log~innovation~variance~(ln~sigma[i]^2)")
  ),
  fixed = c(gamma0_mu_mlts, gamma0_phi_mlts, gamma0_ln_sigma_mlts),
  sd    = c(sigma_mu_mlts, sigma_phi_mlts, sigma_ln_sigma_mlts)
)

# density curves (fixed effect +/- 4 SDs)
re_dens <- re_params |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(
    param = param,
    fixed = fixed,
    sd = sd,
    x = seq(fixed - 4 * sd, fixed + 4 * sd, length.out = 400),
    density = dnorm(x, fixed, sd)
  ) |>
  mutate(in_95 = abs(x - fixed) <= 1.96 * sd)

# labels showing the model-implied distribution
re_labels <- re_params |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("N(%.2f, %.2f²)", fixed, sd))
```

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "35%"}

* Each person has their own $\mu_i$, $\phi_i$, and $\ln(\sigma^2_i)$
* The model assumes these person-specific parameters are **normally distributed** around the fixed effect (mean) with the estimated random effect SD
* The shaded area covers the central 95% of the model-implied parameters
* Example: $\phi_i$ ranges from about `r round(gamma0_phi_mlts - 1.96 * sigma_phi_mlts, 2)` to `r round(gamma0_phi_mlts + 1.96 * sigma_phi_mlts, 2)` $\rightarrow$ people differ substantially in their inertia
* Note the scales: $\ln(\sigma^2_i)$ is on the log-scale, so `exp()` transforms it back to a variance

:::
:::  {.column width = "5%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "60%"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

ggplot(re_dens, aes(x = x, y = density)) +
  geom_area(
    data = ~ filter(.x, in_95),
    fill = "#4F7F39", alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, color = "#4F7F39") +
  geom_vline(
    data = re_params, aes(xintercept = fixed),
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = re_labels,
    aes(x = fixed, y = Inf, label = label),
    vjust = 2.5, hjust = -1.1, size = 6, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ param, ncol = 1, scales = "free", labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = "Person-specific parameter value", y = "Density") +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## Model Building: Adding Restrictions

```{r}
#| include: false
options(width = 120)  # increase from default ~80
```


* The function `mlts_model(q = 1)` fits a model with random effects for all parameters by default
* There are several arguments that allow to restrict certain parameters to zero
* If we would like to fit a model with restricted innovation variances (i.e., as in `lme4`), we can request this with `mlts_model(..., fix_inno_vars = TRUE)`


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "65%"}


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

mlts_m2 <- mlts_model(q = 1, fix_inno_vars = TRUE)
mlts_m2[, c("Level", "Type", "Param_Label", "isRandom")] # inspect

```

* This deletes the respective correlations from the model as well
* Alternatively, the argument `ranef_zero` accepts a character vector of random effect variances that should be set to zero

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mlts_m2 <- mlts_model(q = 1, ranef_zero = "ln.sigma2_1")
```

* Both result in the same model object

:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mlts_paths(mlts_m2)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
```

## Model Building: Adding Higher Lags

```{r}
#| include: false
options(width = 120)  # increase from default ~80
```


* The function `mlts_model(q = 1)` fits a model with an AR(1) process by default
* The argument `max_lag` allows to include lagged effects of higher order (maximum is 3)
* Dynamic parameters are **random** (vary across individuals) by default and can be fixed by e.g., `fix_dynamics = TRUE` or by specifying their names in the argument `ranef_zero = ...`
* Fitting a model with AR(2) structure and fixed innovation variances:

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "65%"}


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

mlts_m3 <- mlts_model(q = 1, max_lag = 2, fix_inno_vars = TRUE)
mlts_m3[, c("Level", "Type", "Param_Label", "isRandom")] # inspect
```

## Assumptions of Vector Autoregressive Models

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "45%"}

* No mean trends in the constructs, i.e., the time-series is **stationary** [@McNeish2020]
  * Can be tested graphically or, e.g., with a linear growth model
  * If violated, consider detrending or residual DSEM
* Equal time intervals between measurements (otherwise, $\phi$-parameters can be biased)
  * If violated, use `tinterval`-function to insert missing data in between measurements

```{r}
  , c("id", "timepoint", "time_window", "time_diff")])
```

## Handling Unequally Spaced Measurements

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "35%"}

* Our data structure treats the observations as if the time interval between measurements is equal
* Solution: we need to add rows to the data such that the intervals between rows correspond to the same time lag
* The added rows are filled with `NA` on the respective construct and then "imputed" while fitting
* The exact procedure for our particular data set can be found in the accompanying R script `prepare_bolzen.R`
* In general, you need a variable that contains integer or continuous time (at least the distance between values has to be meaningful)
* More in Practical Aspects




:::
:::  {.column width = "5%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "60%"}

:::: {.columns}

* The very top of `summary(mlts_fit3)` reports the **convergence checks** of `rstan`
* The model with AR(2) effects gets flagged here
* To make sense of these warnings, we need to understand what happens "under the hood" of the estimation

### Short Detour: Bayesian estimation with MCMC

* How does the sampler work?
* How do we check that it worked?

## Bayesian Estimation in a Nutshell


* Bayesian estimation combines what we know **before** seeing the data (prior) with what the data tell us (likelihood)
* The result is not a single point estimate, but a whole distribution: the **posterior**

$$
\underbrace{p(\theta \mid y)}_{\text{posterior}} \;\propto\; \underbrace{p(y \mid \theta)}_{\text{likelihood}} \; \underbrace{p(\theta)}_{\text{prior}}
$$


* In our model, $\theta$ contains
  * the fixed effects (e.g., $\mu$, $\phi(1)$, $\phi(2)$)
  * the random effect SDs and correlations
  * the person-specific parameters of all $N = `r length(unique(bolzen_baseline$id))`$ persons
* The posterior is a distribution over **all of these parameters at once**
* For such a multilevel time-series model, we cannot write down this posterior in closed form

#### A short note on priors

<!-- * Setting priors is a fundamental part in a Bayesian analysis -->
* In `mlts`, we set **weakly informative** priors by default for all model parameters
* If you have justified assumptions about a certain range of parameter values, you can encode this knowledge by changing the prior distributions

---

## Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

# idealized illustration: draws from a posterior (here: N(0.57, 0.03))
set.seed(2026)
draws_n <- c(10, 100, 1000, 10000)
draws_df <- map_dfr(
  draws_n,
  ~ tibble(n = .x, value = rnorm(.x, mean = 0.57, sd = 0.03))
) |>
  mutate(n = factor(n, levels = draws_n, labels = paste0(format(draws_n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), " draws")))

curve_df <- tibble(
  value = seq(0.45, 0.69, length.out = 300),
  density = dnorm(value, 0.57, 0.03)
)
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

# toy random-walk Metropolis sampler for a posterior N(0.57, 0.03)
metropolis <- function(start, n = 500, step = 0.03, mu = 0.57, sd = 0.03) {
  x <- numeric(n)
  cur <- start
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    prop <- cur + rnorm(1, 0, step)
    log_ratio <- dnorm(prop, mu, sd, log = TRUE) - dnorm(cur, mu, sd, log = TRUE)
    if (log(runif(1)) < log_ratio) cur <- prop
    x[i] <- cur
  }
  x
}

set.seed(2026)
starts <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 0.95)
toy_chains <- imap_dfr(
  starts,
  function(s, k) tibble(
    chain = factor(paste("Chain", k)),
    iteration = 1:500,
    value = metropolis(s)
  )
)
n_warmup_toy <- 100
```

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "50%"}

* Instead of calculating the posterior, we **draw samples** from it
* A sampler (a "Markov chain") moves through the parameter space and visits regions in proportion to their posterior probability
* Everything we report is a **summary of the draws**:
  * posterior mean, SD, and credible intervals (`Mean`, `SD`, `2.5%`, `97.5%` in the `summary()`)
  * the more (good) draws, the better the approximation

#### Chains, warmup, and draws
  
* Samplers are started several times from different (random) starting values: **chains**
* At the start, chains have not yet found the region of high posterior probability $\rightarrow$ **warmup** (the first draws are discarded)
* After warmup, all chains should wander around the same region and look like a "fat hairy caterpillar"
* If chains do **not** agree with each other, they have not converged $\rightarrow$ we cannot trust the draws

:::
:::  {.column width = "2%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "48%"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| out-width: "90%"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center

ggplot(draws_df, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 30, fill = "#4F7F39", alpha = 0.4, color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = curve_df, aes(y = density),
    linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ n, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Parameter value", y = NULL,
    caption = "Dashed line: true posterior; bars: histogram of the draws"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| out-width: "90%"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center

ggplot(toy_chains, aes(x = iteration, y = value, color = chain)) +
  annotate(
    "rect", xmin = 0, xmax = n_warmup_toy, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = n_warmup_toy / 2, y = 0.95, label = "warmup",
    size = 6, color = "grey30"
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#4F7F39", "#1F77B4", "#E69F00", "#B2182B")) +
  labs(
    x = "Iteration", y = "Parameter value", color = NULL,
    caption = "Toy example: 4 chains of a simple Metropolis sampler"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```



:::
::::


## MCMC in `mlts`

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "40%"}

* `mlts` uses `rstan`, i.e., the sampler of Stan (a variant of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo called **NUTS**)
* With `iter = 2000` and the default of 2 chains
  * the first 1000 iterations of each chain are warmup (discarded)
  * the last 1000 iterations of each chain are kept
  * $\rightarrow$ 2,000 post-warmup draws per parameter
* The `summary()` is based on these 2,000 draws
* Traceplots show whether the chains mix well

:::
:::  {.column width = "2%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "58%"}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mlts_fit3 <- mlts_fit(
  ...,
  iter = 2000,  # default: 500
  chains = 2    # default: 2
)

rstan::traceplot(mlts_fit3$stanfit,
                 pars = "gammas")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center

rstan::traceplot(mlts_fit3$stanfit,
                 pars = "gammas")
```

:::
::::

---

## How Do We Know the Sampler Worked?

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "40%"}

#### Convergence diagnostics

Reported at the top of the `summary()`:

* **Rhat** ($\hat{R}$, potential scale reduction factor): compares the variance between and within chains
  * Should be close to 1 (here: $< 1.01$)
* **ESS** (effective sample size, bulk and tail): draws of a Markov chain are autocorrelated, so 2,000 draws are worth fewer independent draws
  * Should be large enough (here: $> 200$, i.e., 100 per chain)
* **Divergent transitions**: the sampler had trouble exploring the posterior
  * Should be 0
  

:::
:::  {.column width = "5%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "55%"}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

summary(mlts_fit3)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

summary_lines <- capture.output(summary(mlts_fit3))
cat(summary_lines[1:10], sep = "\n")
cat("[...]")
```

#### Back to our AR(2) model

* The warnings we see for `mlts_fit3` tell us which of these checks failed (Bulk and Tail ESS are below 200 for at least one parameter)
* This does **not** automatically mean the model is useless, but we should be careful with interpreting the results
* In this specific case, it is probably enough to run more iterations of the Markov chain to get a higher ESS

:::
::::
